before:
The airport for Guanacaste and the Pacific coast, 11 km west of Liberia, and the tourism gateway for the west of Costa Rica. It is one of four international airports in the country, and the one that puts clients nearest the Pacific beaches.

The terminal is modern. A new 23,000 square metre building opened in January 2012 under a twenty year concession, replacing the older facility on the same site.

The runway is 2,750 metres and takes wide body aircraft up to a 747, which is what allows large aircraft to come in directly rather than feeding through a connection.

The site covers 243 hectares.
after:
The airport for Guanacaste and the tourism gateway for the north west of Costa Rica, about 11 km west of Liberia. It is one of four international airports in the country. According to the Costa Rica Tourism Board, it connects with beaches in one of the country's largest tourist areas and mainly receives flights for tourists visiting Guanacaste, Monteverde and La Fortuna.

The terminal is modern. A new 23,000 square metre building opened in January 2012 under a twenty year concession.

The runway is 2,750 metres and takes wide body aircraft up to a 747, which is what allows large aircraft to come in directly rather than feeding through a connection.

Its site covers 243 hectares.

claims.note: No archived copy exists for this airport, so source 1 is the article as it reads today (revised 23 September 2026). The Tourism Board lists it as Liberia's airport for Guanacaste and the FCDO places it in Guanacaste. The official website in Wikipedia's infobox (guanacastecrairport.com) answers with a Wix 'domain not connected' page on both hosts, and liberiacrairport.com, which Wikipedia also cites, is a tours, hotels and shuttles site, not the operator, so neither is used.

claims.claim: FCDO: services at Liberia airport have been subject to interruptions
claims.why: Held back: the FCDO's Costa Rica page (still current at 23 September 2026, last updated 19 May 2026) says services at Liberia airport have been subject to interruptions and that travellers should carefully monitor information from their travel provider when travelling to and from it. It replaces nothing in the old text, and no second source says what the interruptions were (DGAC's notices list shows nothing on the airport). Recommended for Andy: it is the one current warning specific to this airport, and could go in as an attributed sentence.

claims.claim: flights mostly North American; TUI charters from Gatwick
claims.why: Held back: DGAC's 2024 airline table for the airport is led by United (430,231 international passengers) and American (421,492), then Delta, Alaska, Southwest, WestJet, JetBlue and Air Canada, with TUI Airways (12,288) and Edelweiss (10,702) the only European airlines; 915,126 of 926,157 arriving international passengers came from North America. The UK CAA counts only charter passengers between the UK and Liberia, all at Gatwick: 7,251 in 2025, down from 12,223 in 2024. New facts that replace nothing; recommended for Andy, since the UK link is what an agent needs.
